newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: RUGBY UNION-JONES FEELS FOR BIGGEST RIVAL EALES.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-JONES FEELS FOR BIGGEST RIVAL EALES.

text.p: DUNEDIN, Aug 13 - All Black Ian Jones is sorry his biggest rival in test rugby, John Eales, has been invalided out of the test at Carisbrook on Saturday, NZPA reports.

"It's a shame he won't be playing, a big blow to the Aussies but it's happened early in the week and they should be able to adapt," Jones said last night after Eales, along with Matt Cockbain, were ruled out of the tri-series test.
"He's a very serious competitor and a lot of the Wallaby game is based around him because of his strength in set pieces like the lineout and the kickoffs."
Eales and Jones have been two of the best lineout jumpers in test rugby for a number of years.

Their's was a duel within a duel keenly awaited by the sold-out 42,000 crowd for the match that doubles as the Bledisloe Cup test. New Zealand have taken an unassailable lead in the cup series, winning the first two of three tests, and has a firm grip on the tri-series.
Australia have been torn by injuries, with Eales and Cockbain being the latest in a long list that includes Daniel Manu, Tim Horan, Matthew Burke and Pat Howard.
"I guess when one door closes for one player, it opens up for another," North Harbour captain Jones said.
ACT Brumbies star John Langford will make his Wallaby debut in place of lineout leaper Eales and Fili Finau comes in for Cockbain.
"No doubt he's inspired to do well and he's got Brumbies all around him in the team," Jones said of Langford, a surprising choice ahead of regular squad member Garrick Morgan.
"It'll be a big occasion for him, it'll be huge. He's got nothing to lose so he'll go out and play well."
Eales has good memories of Carisbrook, where he marked his test debut with a try against Scotland seven seasons ago.
"It's fantastic to play there again. The crowd is always very supportive."

The All Blacks also lost a player to injury yesterday. Reserve hooker Norm Hewitt tore calf muscles in a scrummaging session and has been replaced in the squad by Otago's stand-in captain Anton Oliver.
